THE TWO-BOOK BANK

By: Este de Klerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The men who gave a new meaning to bank robbery. In what is described as one of the most daring heists SA has ever seen, how exactly was almost R2 billion looted?

Unique Selling Point:
The men who gave a new meaning to bank robbery. In what is described as one of the most daring heists SA has ever seen, how exactly was almost R2 billion looted, fictitious accounts and overdrafts created and how was the majority of shares in the bank bought with non-existing money?

It takes a masterplan for a heist to succeed. Meticulous and detailed planning. The right move at the exact right time. Roleplayers have to come together to successfully execute the plan -- each one playing their own part.
Putting together the pieces in what ultimately lead to the collapse of VBS reads like a movie script – the masterplan for a successful heist.

We will do a story on who the kingpin and roleplayers are, how they planned the heist, how they executed it, how it worked, how much money was stolen, in which manner it was stolen, from whom it was stolen. We will compare the lavish lifestyles of the perpetrators against those from whom were stolen - now left in the dark and destitute. What are those on the ground who have lost everything saying and is there any recourse for them?
What happens now - will there be prosecution?

Summary:
In 1982, VBS was established as the Venda Building Society -
as a mutual fund in which one could deposit savings or buy shares.
VBS came to prominence in 2016 when it granted a R7.8 million loan to former president Jacob Zuma to settle debt relating to the upgrades to his Nkandla home.
Despite the Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA) forbidding municipalities to invest with mutual banks, many did. In early 2017, Treasury issued an instruction to municipalities to stop investing with the institution. As a result, a number of councils withdrew more than R1 billion from the bank.
The Reserve Bank in March this year and put the bank under curatorship amid a liquidity crisis. In April this year, the Reserve Bank of SA launched an investigation under the leadership of adv Terry Motau SC en the firm Werksmans.
A provisional report into fraud, probable money laundering and reckless business practices found that around 53 individuals unjustifiably and illegally received R1,89 billion between 2015 and 2018 and calls for them to be criminally charged, the money be recovered and VBS be closed.

“It is corrupt and rotten to the core. Indeed, there is hardly a person in its employ in any position of authority who is not, in some way or other, complicit,” adv Motau said.

The report states that “the overwhelming evidence that has been gathered, from numerous sources, reveals (VBS chairperson Tshifhiwa) Matodzi be the kingpin in the fraudulent and theftuous conduct of VBS’ business. He, his companies, and his associates have been positively identified as the main beneficiaries of the massive fraud”.

According to the Curator’s application to liquidate Vele Investments, “the bank has been the victim of a large scale fraud that has caused the bank a losss in excess of at least R1,5 billion and Vele has participated in and benefitted from the aforesaid fraud”. (p12)



Further information:
FRAUDULENT SCHEME OF EPIC PROPROTIONS
The curator, Anoosh Rooplal noted: “More egregious than the perpetration of a fraudulent scheme of such enormity, is that the Fraudulent Scheme was orchestrated by the highest ranking officials at VBS.

WHO ARE THE MAIN PERPETRATORS

These five members have been main perpetrators:
Tshifiwa Calvin Matodzi - chairman of VBS’s board of directors
Andile Malusi Attwell Ramavhunga - VBS CEO
Philippus (Philip) Nicholas Truter - VBS CFO
Phopi Londolani Mukhodobwane - VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management
Mmbulani Robert Madzonga - VBS former COO

These five -- the Big Five -- acted individually and in concert with one another.

Matodzi was the main architect - and assured Rooplal that he, personally and Vele in which he served as a director and chairman, benefitted the most from the Fraudulent Scheme.

Vele Investments benefitted in an amount of at least R1 507 000 000.

WHO ARE THE VICTIMS

The victims of the Fraudulent Scheme are depositors and other clients of VBS which include the Venda community, businesses and public institutions, including local municipalities and the Public Investment Corporation (PIC).
Rooplal states that the contributors to municipalities are obviously taxpayers, so therefore the SA public has suffered too.

HOW WAS THE MASTERPLAN EXECUTED?

The Motau report says that the entire crooked scheme was supported by two pillars:
The first pillar: the capture and looting of VBS
The second pillar: the fraudulent concealment

The fraudulent scheme was pervasive and as Motau called it, one of the most daring heists the country has ever seen, but it was actually quite unsophisticated.

TRUTER (CFO) & MUKHODOBWANE VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management), at the behest of the five perpetrators, manually created the illusion of deposits being made into VBS.

They used the VBS Bank’s electronic accounting system to create fictitious General Ledger entries and have those entries reflect as “deposits” in the VBS bank accounts chosen and created by and for the five perpetrators and their associated entities - which include Vele, Matodzi, Ramavhunga and Madzonga

TRUTER & MUKHODOBWANE transferred the “deposited” funds from VBS “suspense account” to another VBS account held by one or more of the perpetrators, their associated entities or parties related to them. As an alternative to this method, fictitious entries were at times created in the actual VBS account of an entity

Once these “deposits” appeared in a VBS account, the account holder (who comprised the perpetrators, their associated entities or related parties) was enabled to draw on the deposit. As such, real money -- that had been entrusted to the bank by the victims of the Fraudulent Scheme, ie municipalities) became available to the perpetrators, overdrafts were cleared and funds could be transferred out of such accounts

Motau found that the contract financing was a prime location of the looting of the funds of VBS. “Astonishingly, the contract finance book, which eventually became the single largest asset of VBS was not recorded in the bank’s operating system, but was simply recorded on an Excel spreadsheet which could be manipulated with ease.
“The inescapable inference that must be drawn from this is that it better suited the interest of those who sought to manipulate VBS’ banking systems for their own benefit to keep contract finance off the operating system.”

WHOSE MONEY WAS USED?

This fraudulent mechanism provided the perpetrators and their associated entities, including Vele, with money which was predominantly made of deposits held by the bank on behalf of members of the public and municipalities. THIS, they used to fund their lifestyles, purchase immovable property, buy high-end motor vehicles and take up shares and interests in other entities.

CATEGORIES OF FRAUDULENT TRANSACTIONS PERPETRATED THROUGH SCHEME

VELE’S INSURE ACQUISITION: R250 MILLION
Vele fraudulently acquired an investment in Insure Group Managers (Pty) Ltd for an amount of R250 million. The acquisition was funded by VBS through the Fraudulent Scheme - in other words, Vele paid nothing for the investment. (add more to this paragraphs 108 - 115)

2. VELE’S PURPORTED SHARE UPTAKES IN VBS (R80 MILLION & R90 MILLION)
Vele purported to purchase shares in VBS on two occassions in order to become the majority shareholder:

First: Vele fraudulently misrepresented that an actual R80 million deposit made by Insure into VBS for an unrelated purpose, was payment of the purchase price in respect of a share subscription in VBS. Neither Vele, nor Insure on its behalf, paid any money For the shares.
Second: Vele purported to subscribe for further shares in VBS, by paying the amount of R90 million with the proceeds for a fictitious deposit of R350 million created through the Fraudulent Scheme. Again, Vele paid nothing for these shares.

Motau stated that Vele was an “ostensible” shareholder shareholder in VBS.
He found that during 2017 Vele purported to take up a 53% shareholding in VBS. This was purportedly in terms of a rights issue. Vele, which was not an existing shareholder at the time of the rights issue, was therefore not entitled to take up any shares on offer. However, Vele managed to convince the board of directors of VBS to accept an amount of R80 million as an equity investment against the issue of a majority shareholding. In truth, Vele invested absolutely nothing into VBS and it acquired the shares by a blatant fraud.
(See further Motau report page 58 & 59)

3. FRAUDULENT OVERDRAFT PAYMENTS: R262 MILLION
The Fraudulent Scheme was used to clear - or repay - the outstanding overdraft facilities in respect of Matodzi, other perpetrators and their associated entities in an amount of approximately R262 million. These fraudulent transactions which will also be referenced as the “Eagle Canyon List” (so named after the meeting at Eagle Canyon where Matodzi instructed the clearing of overdrafts). (more in paragraphs 116 - 289)

Motau noted (p 57) there are many examples of vehicle finance facilities and mortgage bond facilities granted to associates and parties related to Vele and Matodzi where few, if any, monthly instalments were honoured. There are also very large overdraft facilities where no amounts were ever paid into the accounts and the facility limits simply increased to permit the escalating out flows.

4. Fraudulent deposits: R929 925 280.46
Fraudulently created deposits were made through the Fraudelent Scheme to several of the perpetrators and their associated entities. Vele was the recipient of the bulk of these fraudulent deposits in the amount of R745 million.

WHY THE BANK GOT INTO TROUBLE

The deficit created by the perpetrators grew larger as the perpetrators were effectively stealing money at a greater rate than was being deposited into VBS.
THIS resulted in the severe liquidity crisis in which VBS found itself - which the perpetrators sought to hide in VBS’ 2017 Annual Financial Statements audited by KPMG.

The corruption was so deeply entrenched amongst the perpetrators at VBS that they resorted to obtaining deposits into the bank from municipalities by paying officials “commissions” on funds deposited by municipalities into VBS. These bribes were channelled through Robvet (pty) Ltd.

-- THE LIMPOPO LINK

The provincial government of Limpopo has its own internal investigation into how municipal moneys were siphoned into VBS even though the Municipal Finance Mangement Act forbids municipalities from investing money in a mutual bank.

ANC Limpopo Treasurer Danny Msiza and ANC Limpopo Deputy Chairperson Florence Radzilani is implicated in the Motau report.
The motau report states that during the investigation, Phopi Londolani Mukhodobwane - VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management - testified, that the kingpin in the so-called “commission agent” scheme was Msiza.
It is said that Msiza that commission of 2-3% for soliciting municipality agents to deposit money with VBS Bank.
Limpopo ANC Spokesperson Ntshaveni Khumbudzo (060-769-0338) said that its internal report would only be complete at the end of November. They say they will act against officials implicated.

FURTHER ATTEMPTS TO SAVE THE BANK FROM IMPLODING

Further attempts were made to obtain deposits from the PIC and PRASA (R1 billion).

The Motau report states:
To avoid the bank from imploding after municipalities withdrew deposits, VBS went on an ambitious campaign to attract other large deposits from municipalities and state-owed entities like the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) and shifted towards aggressive, high-risk lending.

During the investigation, key witness General Manager of Treasury at VBS, Phopi Mukhodobwane, testified that VBS had attempted to solicit R1-billion from Prasa in late 2017.
The report states that Mukhodobwane testified that a “commission” - read “bribe” - of R1,5-million was paid to a group of union officials from Satawu who claimed to be able to facilitate such a large deposit from Prasa. The plan was stymied thanks to an unrelated investigation into Prasa.

Mukhodobwane himself stole R30-million from the bank, Motau and Werksmans found.

Press Release:


VBS – The Two Book bank
From building societies to municipalities, millions of rands were deposited into VBS Mutual bank – only for it to be plundered by its executives. In just over three years, almost R2 billion was quietly siphoned off in what’s been called one of the more daring bank heists South Africa has ever seen. But how did bank insiders manage to loot the bank for so long without being detected? Carte Blanche follows the money.
Producer: Este de Klerk
Presenter: Derek Watts
Researchers: Siniketiwe Hlanze and Tony Beamish


Script:


VBS: THE TWO BOOK BANK

PRODUCER: ESTE DE KLERK
PRESENTER: DEREK WATTS
EDITOR: ROBIN LEUCI

VO: Forty-eight-year-old Funani Ndou, a single-mother of three lives in the rural village of Luwamondo, an hour's drive outside Thohoyandou. Over the past few months, she's been consumed with worry about her children's future.

FUNANI: My husband's pension came here at VBS, it was only 130.

VO: In 18 years, Funani's investment grew to R300 000.

DEREK: Were you satisfied that you could look after your family with R300 000?

FUNANI: Yes, I was satisfied that my money grew up.

VO: Funani is one of 17 300 retail clients swindled by the Venda Building Society - now known as VBS Mutual Bank.

DEREK WATTS: Launched in 1982, VBS didn't exactly set the business world alight. By 2014, it was still a modest, but financially struggling bank, taking deposits from individuals, stokvels and burial societies.

VO: Then, VBS executives embarked on a turnaround strategy to change the bank into a profit-making enterprise by obtaining very large, but short-term, deposits from municipalities.

FUNANI:

DEREK:

FUNANI:

VO: Funani lost R200 000 of his investment and needs to find a job, a difficult task in this area.

FUNANI: I don't know what I am going to do. Wanted to send my son to college, but couldnt….

VO: Since the release of "The Great Bank Heist" report written by advocate Terry Motau, SC, appointed by the South African Reserve Bank to investigate alleged fraud and reckless business practices at VBS, more and more details HAVE emerged over the past week of just how blatantly R1,89 billion was looted and distributed by VBS's top executives to themselves, their companies and beneficiaries linked to them.

Money was stolen from the poorest of the poor - people we found in Makhado and Thohoyandou in Limpopo where two of VBS' five branches are situated.

DEREK LINK: These are VBS clients queueing up here at Nedbank from early morning. They are hoping for a limited payment which has been reserved by the Reserve Bank from National Treasury.

VO: The Treasury guaranteed and capped payments to R100 000.
Under the guidance of Anoosh Rooplal, VBS was then placed under curatorship by the Reserve Bank, to try and restore and fix VBS from its liquidity crisis.

ANOOSH ROOPLAL: VBS bank had reached a settlement obligation on the National Payment System. that is where there's settlement between banks in South Africa and VBS had a settlement breach. things weren't answered to the satisfaction of the prudential authority and that then led to the bank being placed into curatorship.

VO: But red flags popped up during Rooplal's investigation.

ANOOSH ROOPLAL: I picked up various irregularities - gross mismanagement of the bank, various breaches of governance I made the recommendation to the prudential authority to appoint the investigator. That was Advocate Terry Motau.

VO: Advocate Motau states the liquidity crisis was "the result of the wholescale theft of the bank's funds".

DEREK LINK: The report says that more than 50 people benefitted from gratuitous payments over the last three years and that there is hardly a person at VBS employed in an authoritative position that isn't complicit in one way or another.

VO: According to the report, five key individuals - all part of VBS' top management - were complicit.

TSHIFHIWA MATODZI
[on-screen]
VBS: CHAIRMAN OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS
VELE: DIRECTOR & CHAIRMAN OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS

ANDILE RAMAVHUNGA
[on-screen]
VBS: CEO

PHILIP TRUTER
[on-screen]
VBS: CFO

PHOPI MUKHODOBWANE
[on-screen]
VBS: GENERAL HEAD OF TREASURY

ROBERT MADZONGA
[on-screen]
VBS: FORMER COO
VELE: DIRECTOR
FORMER COO
CEO

VO: Advocate Motau states in his report:

[MOTAU REPORT] "The overwhelming evidence that has been gathered, reveals Matodzi to be the kingpin in the fraudulent and theftuous conduct of VBS' business. He, his companies, and his associates have been positively identified as the main beneficiaries of the massive fraud."

DEREK LINK: Mr Matodzi initially agreed to an interview but cancelled earlier this week. According to his lawyer he has been bombarded by the media which had made bold, false and sweeping statements amidst an ongoing criminal investigation.

VO: In contrast to the Municipal Finance Management Act, municipalities, such as the Dr Ruth S Mompati District Municipality in Northwest with its seat in Vryburg, illegally invested money with VBS bank.
Between 2015 and 2018, VBS received R3,4 billion from municipalities.

HOW WAS THE PLAN EXECUTED?

VO: But how was the plan executed?
A fictitious depositor is entered into the books of VBS using a suspense - or temporary - account used for unknown entries.
This is a paper transaction. The balancing entry is recorded on an Excel Spreadsheet and not in the bank's official accounting system.
VBS then gets real money as a deposit from an entity such as a municipality.
The fictitious depositor then withdraws the real money paid in by the municipality.
VBS then owes this money to the municipality - because in short, the fictitious depositor stole it.

Forensic auditor, Andre Prakke, honed in on the detail of the report.

DEREK: Now they were running two books, effectively.

ANDRE PRAKKE: Book 1, if we can call it that, was the real book. The loans and the bonds and the stuff that they lent to the public. Book 2 was the one that was a counter-entry to the fictitious deposits to make the fictitious ones balance. And the balance of that one was brought into Book 1 so the whole banking book would balance the balance sheet.

DEREK: So which book do you show to the auditors?

ANDRE PRAKKE: Both books were shown. The auditor didn't look at Book 2 and didn't do any test on it. It's also clear from the investigator's report.

VO: Advocate Motau referred to "Book 2" as the contract finance book.

[MOTAU REPORT] Astonishingly, the contract finance book, which eventually became the single largest asset of VBS was not recorded in the bank's operating system but was simply recorded on an Excel spreadsheet which could be manipulated with ease.

VO: Motau found that VBS's auditor -- Sipho Malaba, a KPMG partner played an integral part in the cover-up. He resigned from the firm in April. Motau found that Malaba was aware that there was a cash hole at the bank, but signed off on VBS's 2017 financials irrespective. According to the report, Malaba received almost R34-million.

[MOTAU REPORT] I FIND THAT MALABA COMMITTED FRAUD BY APPROVING AND SIGNING THE REPORT.

VO: Malaba said in a written statement that he is in the process of starting legal action to have the report nullified. He says: "The report is riddled with inaccuracies and hyperbole. Evidence was ignored and the report is tainted by a predetermined outcome."

VO: According to the report, Vele Investments - of which Matodzi and Madzonga are directors - played a central role in the siphoning of money from VBS, to the tune of R936 million.

[MOTAU REPORT] IT EMERGES VERY CLEARLY THAT VBS AND VELE HAVE OPERATED AS A SINGLE CRIMINAL ENTERPRISE WITH MATODZI AT THE HELM.

VO: To rescue VBS from the liquidity crisis, VBS execs came up with ambitious plans in 2017 - trying to solicit a billion-rand investment from the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa and a R2-million investment from the Public Investment Corporation -- but it failed. Agents were also used and paid commissions to connect municipalities with VBS. Some of these "agents" received tens of millions according to the Motau report.

VO: In July this year, Rooplal started civil proceedings to recover some of the money.
Vele Investments was liquidated - and the top five VBS execs have been provisionally sequestrated -- declared insolvent -- and their assets frozen. [go back to character spider web]

ANOOSH: This is really building to ensuring that assets can be preserved and not further dissipated in the process.

DEREK: So you can't sell your expensive house or your Lamborghini or Rolls or new Merc?

ANOOSH: That's how the law is designed to work. (check audio)

VO: Matodzi received R325 million; Mukhodobwane and Madzonga each R30 million; Ramavhunga almost R29 million. Truter testified he was promised a R5-million bonus, but only received 2-million.
They all declined the opportunity to respond.

DEREK LINK: Despite the pictures of his wife draped over expensive cars, a helicopter and a boat, Robert Madzonga has protested his innocence. Advocate Motau said he could find no definitive role that he played, but say that his denial of any knowledge or his involvement in the fraud or theft rings hollow.

VO: In direct contrast to these lavish lifestyles, there are those who now have to bear the brunt of the brazen scheme

The Dr Ruth S Mompati District Municipality invested a total of R150 million with VBS. This money was earmarked for the upgrade of crucial infrastructure such as water waste, sanitation and sewerage lines.

Back in Thohoyandou, Funani says her future looks bleak.

DEREK: Funani, tell us how you feel right now?

FUNANI: I am very angry….

VO: VBS's future is uncertain and 94 of the 125 employees were retrenched.
It's now up to the NPA and the Hawks to continue the criminal investigation.

But this was Motau's wish:
[MOTAU REPORT]: I TRUST, IN THIS CASE, ARRESTS WILL BE MADE.

-- END --

PROMOS

PROMO 1: 30"
It's been described as one of the most daring heists South Africa has ever seen. But exactly how did VBS executives manage to loot R1,89 billion from the bank.

ANDRE PRAKKE: You need a well-structured, thought out, planned way of doing it. And it's very clear from the Reserve Bank's report that this is exactly what happened.

Municipalities, burial societies and retail depositors have all been robbed.

FUNANI: I don't know what I am going to do. I have no money to feed my family.

PROMO 2: 15"
What is a little bribery and corruption between business associates?
According to advocate Terry Motau's report into alleged fraud at VBS Mutual Bank, almost R2 billion was looted as a result of it.

FUNANI: We don't get our money and we don't know where it is.

PROMO 3: 15"
It's been called one of the most daring heists in the country, but how was almost R2 billion looted and the alleged fraud concealed for so long? We hone in on how VBS execs masterminded and executed the plan and why their house of cards eventually collapsed.

PROMO 4:10"
Billions were stolen from from the poorest of the poor, municipalities, burial societies and stokvels. But how did VBS executives almost get away with it?

We will do a story on who the kingpin and roleplayers are, how they planned the heist, how they executed it, how it worked, how much money was stolen, in which manner it was stolen, from whom it was stolen. We will compare the lavish lifestyles of the perpetrators against those from whom were stolen - now left in the dark and destitute. What are those on the ground who have lost everything saying and is there any recourse for them? What happens now - will there be prosecution? Summary: In 1982, VBS was established as the Venda Building Society - as a mutual fund in which one could deposit savings or buy shares. VBS came to prominence in 2016 when it granted a R7.8 million loan to former president Jacob Zuma to settle debt relating to the upgrades to his Nkandla home. Despite the Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA) forbidding municipalities to invest with mutual banks, many did. In early 2017, Treasury issued an instruction to municipalities to stop investing with the institution. As a result, a number of councils withdrew more than R1 billion from the bank. The Reserve Bank in March this year and put the bank under curatorship amid a liquidity crisis. In April this year, the Reserve Bank of SA launched an investigation under the leadership of adv Terry Motau SC en the firm Werksmans. A provisional report into fraud, probable money laundering and reckless business practices found that around 53 individuals unjustifiably and illegally received R1,89 billion between 2015 and 2018 and calls for them to be criminally charged, the money be recovered and VBS be closed. “It is corrupt and rotten to the core. Indeed, there is hardly a person in its employ in any position of authority who is not, in some way or other, complicit,” adv Motau said. The report states that “the overwhelming evidence that has been gathered, from numerous sources, reveals (VBS chairperson Tshifhiwa) Matodzi be the kingpin in the fraudulent and theftuous conduct of VBS’ business. He, his companies, and his associates have been positively identified as the main beneficiaries of the massive fraud”. According to the Curator’s application to liquidate Vele Investments, “the bank has been the victim of a large scale fraud that has caused the bank a losss in excess of at least R1,5 billion and Vele has participated in and benefitted from the aforesaid fraud”. (p12) Further information: FRAUDULENT SCHEME OF EPIC PROPROTIONS The curator, Anoosh Rooplal noted: “More egregious than the perpetration of a fraudulent scheme of such enormity, is that the Fraudulent Scheme was orchestrated by the highest ranking officials at VBS. WHO ARE THE MAIN PERPETRATORS These five members have been main perpetrators: Tshifiwa Calvin Matodzi - chairman of VBS’s board of directors Andile Malusi Attwell Ramavhunga - VBS CEO Philippus (Philip) Nicholas Truter - VBS CFO Phopi Londolani Mukhodobwane - VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management Mmbulani Robert Madzonga - VBS former COO These five -- the Big Five -- acted individually and in concert with one another. Matodzi was the main architect - and assured Rooplal that he, personally and Vele in which he served as a director and chairman, benefitted the most from the Fraudulent Scheme. Vele Investments benefitted in an amount of at least R1 507 000 000. WHO ARE THE VICTIMS The victims of the Fraudulent Scheme are depositors and other clients of VBS which include the Venda community, businesses and public institutions, including local municipalities and the Public Investment Corporation (PIC). Rooplal states that the contributors to municipalities are obviously taxpayers, so therefore the SA public has suffered too. HOW WAS THE MASTERPLAN EXECUTED? The Motau report says that the entire crooked scheme was supported by two pillars: The first pillar: the capture and looting of VBS The second pillar: the fraudulent concealment The fraudulent scheme was pervasive and as Motau called it, one of the most daring heists the country has ever seen, but it was actually quite unsophisticated. TRUTER (CFO) & MUKHODOBWANE VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management), at the behest of the five perpetrators, manually created the illusion of deposits being made into VBS. They used the VBS Bank’s electronic accounting system to create fictitious General Ledger entries and have those entries reflect as “deposits” in the VBS bank accounts chosen and created by and for the five perpetrators and their associated entities - which include Vele, Matodzi, Ramavhunga and Madzonga TRUTER & MUKHODOBWANE transferred the “deposited” funds from VBS “suspense account” to another VBS account held by one or more of the perpetrators, their associated entities or parties related to them. As an alternative to this method, fictitious entries were at times created in the actual VBS account of an entity Once these “deposits” appeared in a VBS account, the account holder (who comprised the perpetrators, their associated entities or related parties) was enabled to draw on the deposit. As such, real money -- that had been entrusted to the bank by the victims of the Fraudulent Scheme, ie municipalities) became available to the perpetrators, overdrafts were cleared and funds could be transferred out of such accounts Motau found that the contract financing was a prime location of the looting of the funds of VBS. “Astonishingly, the contract finance book, which eventually became the single largest asset of VBS was not recorded in the bank’s operating system, but was simply recorded on an Excel spreadsheet which could be manipulated with ease. “The inescapable inference that must be drawn from this is that it better suited the interest of those who sought to manipulate VBS’ banking systems for their own benefit to keep contract finance off the operating system.” WHOSE MONEY WAS USED? This fraudulent mechanism provided the perpetrators and their associated entities, including Vele, with money which was predominantly made of deposits held by the bank on behalf of members of the public and municipalities. THIS, they used to fund their lifestyles, purchase immovable property, buy high-end motor vehicles and take up shares and interests in other entities. CATEGORIES OF FRAUDULENT TRANSACTIONS PERPETRATED THROUGH SCHEME VELE’S INSURE ACQUISITION: R250 MILLION Vele fraudulently acquired an investment in Insure Group Managers (Pty) Ltd for an amount of R250 million. The acquisition was funded by VBS through the Fraudulent Scheme - in other words, Vele paid nothing for the investment. (add more to this paragraphs 108 - 115) 2. VELE’S PURPORTED SHARE UPTAKES IN VBS (R80 MILLION & R90 MILLION) Vele purported to purchase shares in VBS on two occassions in order to become the majority shareholder: First: Vele fraudulently misrepresented that an actual R80 million deposit made by Insure into VBS for an unrelated purpose, was payment of the purchase price in respect of a share subscription in VBS. Neither Vele, nor Insure on its behalf, paid any money For the shares. Second: Vele purported to subscribe for further shares in VBS, by paying the amount of R90 million with the proceeds for a fictitious deposit of R350 million created through the Fraudulent Scheme. Again, Vele paid nothing for these shares. Motau stated that Vele was an “ostensible” shareholder shareholder in VBS. He found that during 2017 Vele purported to take up a 53% shareholding in VBS. This was purportedly in terms of a rights issue. Vele, which was not an existing shareholder at the time of the rights issue, was therefore not entitled to take up any shares on offer. However, Vele managed to convince the board of directors of VBS to accept an amount of R80 million as an equity investment against the issue of a majority shareholding. In truth, Vele invested absolutely nothing into VBS and it acquired the shares by a blatant fraud. (See further Motau report page 58 & 59) 3. FRAUDULENT OVERDRAFT PAYMENTS: R262 MILLION The Fraudulent Scheme was used to clear - or repay - the outstanding overdraft facilities in respect of Matodzi, other perpetrators and their associated entities in an amount of approximately R262 million. These fraudulent transactions which will also be referenced as the “Eagle Canyon List” (so named after the meeting at Eagle Canyon where Matodzi instructed the clearing of overdrafts). (more in paragraphs 116 - 289) Motau noted (p 57) there are many examples of vehicle finance facilities and mortgage bond facilities granted to associates and parties related to Vele and Matodzi where few, if any, monthly instalments were honoured. There are also very large overdraft facilities where no amounts were ever paid into the accounts and the facility limits simply increased to permit the escalating out flows. 4. Fraudulent deposits: R929 925 280.46 Fraudulently created deposits were made through the Fraudelent Scheme to several of the perpetrators and their associated entities. Vele was the recipient of the bulk of these fraudulent deposits in the amount of R745 million. WHY THE BANK GOT INTO TROUBLE The deficit created by the perpetrators grew larger as the perpetrators were effectively stealing money at a greater rate than was being deposited into VBS. THIS resulted in the severe liquidity crisis in which VBS found itself - which the perpetrators sought to hide in VBS’ 2017 Annual Financial Statements audited by KPMG. The corruption was so deeply entrenched amongst the perpetrators at VBS that they resorted to obtaining deposits into the bank from municipalities by paying officials “commissions” on funds deposited by municipalities into VBS. These bribes were channelled through Robvet (pty) Ltd. -- THE LIMPOPO LINK The provincial government of Limpopo has its own internal investigation into how municipal moneys were siphoned into VBS even though the Municipal Finance Mangement Act forbids municipalities from investing money in a mutual bank. ANC Limpopo Treasurer Danny Msiza and ANC Limpopo Deputy Chairperson Florence Radzilani is implicated in the Motau report. The motau report states that during the investigation, Phopi Londolani Mukhodobwane - VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management - testified, that the kingpin in the so-called “commission agent” scheme was Msiza. It is said that Msiza that commission of 2-3% for soliciting municipality agents to deposit money with VBS Bank. Limpopo ANC Spokesperson Ntshaveni Khumbudzo (060-769-0338) said that its internal report would only be complete at the end of November. They say they will act against officials implicated. FURTHER ATTEMPTS TO SAVE THE BANK FROM IMPLODING Further attempts were made to obtain deposits from the PIC and PRASA (R1 billion). The Motau report states: To avoid the bank from imploding after municipalities withdrew deposits, VBS went on an ambitious campaign to attract other large deposits from municipalities and state-owed entities like the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) and shifted towards aggressive, high-risk lending. During the investigation, key witness General Manager of Treasury at VBS, Phopi Mukhodobwane, testified that VBS had attempted to solicit R1-billion from Prasa in late 2017. The report states that Mukhodobwane testified that a “commission” - read “bribe” - of R1,5-million was paid to a group of union officials from Satawu who claimed to be able to facilitate such a large deposit from Prasa. The plan was stymied thanks to an unrelated investigation into Prasa. Mukhodobwane himself stole R30-million from the bank, Motau and Werksmans found. Extra Budget Items: 1. Producer: Este de Klerk Presenter: Derek Watts Researchers: Siniketiwe Hlanze and Tony Beamish Script: VBS: THE TWO BOOK BANK PRODUCER: ESTE DE KLERK PRESENTER: DEREK WATTS EDITOR: ROBIN LEUCI VO: Forty-eight-year-old Funani Ndou, a single-mother of three lives in the rural village of Luwamondo, an hour's drive outside Thohoyandou. Over the past few months, she's been consumed with worry about her children's future. FUNANI: My husband's pension came here at VBS, it was only 130. VO: In 18 years, Funani's investment grew to R300 000. DEREK: Were you satisfied that you could look after your family with R300 000? FUNANI: Yes, I was satisfied that my money grew up. VO: Funani is one of 17 300 retail clients swindled by the Venda Building Society - now known as VBS Mutual Bank. DEREK WATTS: Launched in 1982, VBS didn't exactly set the business world alight. By 2014, it was still a modest, but financially struggling bank, taking deposits from individuals, stokvels and burial societies. VO: Then, VBS executives embarked on a turnaround strategy to change the bank into a profit-making enterprise by obtaining very large, but short-term, deposits from municipalities. FUNANI: DEREK: FUNANI: VO: Funani lost R200 000 of his investment and needs to find a job, a difficult task in this area. FUNANI: I don't know what I am going to do. Wanted to send my son to college, but couldnt…. VO: Since the release of "The Great Bank Heist" report written by advocate Terry Motau, SC, appointed by the South African Reserve Bank to investigate alleged fraud and reckless business practices at VBS, more and more details HAVE emerged over the past week of just how blatantly R1,89 billion was looted and distributed by VBS's top executives to themselves, their companies and beneficiaries linked to them. Money was stolen from the poorest of the poor - people we found in Makhado and Thohoyandou in Limpopo where two of VBS' five branches are situated. DEREK LINK: These are VBS clients queueing up here at Nedbank from early morning. They are hoping for a limited payment which has been reserved by the Reserve Bank from National Treasury. VO: The Treasury guaranteed and capped payments to R100 000. Under the guidance of Anoosh Rooplal, VBS was then placed under curatorship by the Reserve Bank, to try and restore and fix VBS from its liquidity crisis. ANOOSH ROOPLAL: VBS bank had reached a settlement obligation on the National Payment System. that is where there's settlement between banks in South Africa and VBS had a settlement breach. things weren't answered to the satisfaction of the prudential authority and that then led to the bank being placed into curatorship. VO: But red flags popped up during Rooplal's investigation. ANOOSH ROOPLAL: I picked up various irregularities - gross mismanagement of the bank, various breaches of governance I made the recommendation to the prudential authority to appoint the investigator. That was Advocate Terry Motau. VO: Advocate Motau states the liquidity crisis was "the result of the wholescale theft of the bank's funds". DEREK LINK: The report says that more than 50 people benefitted from gratuitous payments over the last three years and that there is hardly a person at VBS employed in an authoritative position that isn't complicit in one way or another. VO: According to the report, five key individuals - all part of VBS' top management - were complicit. TSHIFHIWA MATODZI [on-screen] VBS: CHAIRMAN OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS VELE: DIRECTOR & CHAIRMAN OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS ANDILE RAMAVHUNGA [on-screen] VBS: CEO PHILIP TRUTER [on-screen] VBS: CFO PHOPI MUKHODOBWANE [on-screen] VBS: GENERAL HEAD OF TREASURY ROBERT MADZONGA [on-screen] VBS: FORMER COO VELE: DIRECTOR FORMER COO CEO VO: Advocate Motau states in his report: [MOTAU REPORT] "The overwhelming evidence that has been gathered, reveals Matodzi to be the kingpin in the fraudulent and theftuous conduct of VBS' business. He, his companies, and his associates have been positively identified as the main beneficiaries of the massive fraud." DEREK LINK: Mr Matodzi initially agreed to an interview but cancelled earlier this week. According to his lawyer he has been bombarded by the media which had made bold, false and sweeping statements amidst an ongoing criminal investigation. VO: In contrast to the Municipal Finance Management Act, municipalities, such as the Dr Ruth S Mompati District Municipality in Northwest with its seat in Vryburg, illegally invested money with VBS bank. Between 2015 and 2018, VBS received R3,4 billion from municipalities. HOW WAS THE PLAN EXECUTED? VO: But how was the plan executed? A fictitious depositor is entered into the books of VBS using a suspense - or temporary - account used for unknown entries. This is a paper transaction. The balancing entry is recorded on an Excel Spreadsheet and not in the bank's official accounting system. VBS then gets real money as a deposit from an entity such as a municipality. The fictitious depositor then withdraws the real money paid in by the municipality. VBS then owes this money to the municipality - because in short, the fictitious depositor stole it. Forensic auditor, Andre Prakke, honed in on the detail of the report. DEREK: Now they were running two books, effectively. ANDRE PRAKKE: Book 1, if we can call it that, was the real book. The loans and the bonds and the stuff that they lent to the public. Book 2 was the one that was a counter-entry to the fictitious deposits to make the fictitious ones balance. And the balance of that one was brought into Book 1 so the whole banking book would balance the balance sheet. DEREK: So which book do you show to the auditors? ANDRE PRAKKE: Both books were shown. The auditor didn't look at Book 2 and didn't do any test on it. It's also clear from the investigator's report. VO: Advocate Motau referred to "Book 2" as the contract finance book. [MOTAU REPORT] Astonishingly, the contract finance book, which eventually became the single largest asset of VBS was not recorded in the bank's operating system but was simply recorded on an Excel spreadsheet which could be manipulated with ease. VO: Motau found that VBS's auditor -- Sipho Malaba, a KPMG partner played an integral part in the cover-up. He resigned from the firm in April. Motau found that Malaba was aware that there was a cash hole at the bank, but signed off on VBS's 2017 financials irrespective. According to the report, Malaba received almost R34-million. [MOTAU REPORT] I FIND THAT MALABA COMMITTED FRAUD BY APPROVING AND SIGNING THE REPORT. VO: Malaba said in a written statement that he is in the process of starting legal action to have the report nullified. He says: "The report is riddled with inaccuracies and hyperbole. Evidence was ignored and the report is tainted by a predetermined outcome." VO: According to the report, Vele Investments - of which Matodzi and Madzonga are directors - played a central role in the siphoning of money from VBS, to the tune of R936 million. [MOTAU REPORT] IT EMERGES VERY CLEARLY THAT VBS AND VELE HAVE OPERATED AS A SINGLE CRIMINAL ENTERPRISE WITH MATODZI AT THE HELM. VO: To rescue VBS from the liquidity crisis, VBS execs came up with ambitious plans in 2017 - trying to solicit a billion-rand investment from the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa and a R2-million investment from the Public Investment Corporation -- but it failed. Agents were also used and paid commissions to connect municipalities with VBS. Some of these "agents" received tens of millions according to the Motau report. VO: In July this year, Rooplal started civil proceedings to recover some of the money. Vele Investments was liquidated - and the top five VBS execs have been provisionally sequestrated -- declared insolvent -- and their assets frozen. [go back to character spider web] ANOOSH: This is really building to ensuring that assets can be preserved and not further dissipated in the process. DEREK: So you can't sell your expensive house or your Lamborghini or Rolls or new Merc? ANOOSH: That's how the law is designed to work. (check audio) VO: Matodzi received R325 million; Mukhodobwane and Madzonga each R30 million; Ramavhunga almost R29 million. Truter testified he was promised a R5-million bonus, but only received 2-million. They all declined the opportunity to respond. DEREK LINK: Despite the pictures of his wife draped over expensive cars, a helicopter and a boat, Robert Madzonga has protested his innocence. Advocate Motau said he could find no definitive role that he played, but say that his denial of any knowledge or his involvement in the fraud or theft rings hollow. VO: In direct contrast to these lavish lifestyles, there are those who now have to bear the brunt of the brazen scheme The Dr Ruth S Mompati District Municipality invested a total of R150 million with VBS. This money was earmarked for the upgrade of crucial infrastructure such as water waste, sanitation and sewerage lines. Back in Thohoyandou, Funani says her future looks bleak. DEREK: Funani, tell us how you feel right now? FUNANI: I am very angry…. VO: VBS's future is uncertain and 94 of the 125 employees were retrenched. It's now up to the NPA and the Hawks to continue the criminal investigation. But this was Motau's wish: [MOTAU REPORT]: I TRUST, IN THIS CASE, ARRESTS WILL BE MADE. -- END -- PROMOS PROMO 1: 30" It's been described as one of the most daring heists South Africa has ever seen. But exactly how did VBS executives manage to loot R1,89 billion from the bank. ANDRE PRAKKE: You need a well-structured, thought out, planned way of doing it. And it's very clear from the Reserve Bank's report that this is exactly what happened. Municipalities, burial societies and retail depositors have all been robbed. FUNANI: I don't know what I am going to do. I have no money to feed my family. PROMO 2: 15" What is a little bribery and corruption between business associates? According to advocate Terry Motau's report into alleged fraud at VBS Mutual Bank, almost R2 billion was looted as a result of it. FUNANI: We don't get our money and we don't know where it is. PROMO 3: 15" It's been called one of the most daring heists in the country, but how was almost R2 billion looted and the alleged fraud concealed for so long? We hone in on how VBS execs masterminded and executed the plan and why their house of cards eventually collapsed. PROMO 4:10" Billions were stolen from from the poorest of the poor, municipalities, burial societies and stokvels. But how did VBS executives almost get away with it?

WHO ARE THE VICTIMS The victims of the Fraudulent Scheme are depositors and other clients of VBS which include the Venda community, businesses and public institutions, including local municipalities and the Public Investment Corporation (PIC). Rooplal states that the contributors to municipalities are obviously taxpayers, so therefore the SA public has suffered too. HOW WAS THE MASTERPLAN EXECUTED? The Motau report says that the entire crooked scheme was supported by two pillars: The first pillar: the capture and looting of VBS The second pillar: the fraudulent concealment The fraudulent scheme was pervasive and as Motau called it, one of the most daring heists the country has ever seen, but it was actually quite unsophisticated. TRUTER (CFO) & MUKHODOBWANE VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management), at the behest of the five perpetrators, manually created the illusion of deposits being made into VBS. They used the VBS Bank’s electronic accounting system to create fictitious General Ledger entries and have those entries reflect as “deposits” in the VBS bank accounts chosen and created by and for the five perpetrators and their associated entities - which include Vele, Matodzi, Ramavhunga and Madzonga TRUTER & MUKHODOBWANE transferred the “deposited” funds from VBS “suspense account” to another VBS account held by one or more of the perpetrators, their associated entities or parties related to them. As an alternative to this method, fictitious entries were at times created in the actual VBS account of an entity Once these “deposits” appeared in a VBS account, the account holder (who comprised the perpetrators, their associated entities or related parties) was enabled to draw on the deposit. As such, real money -- that had been entrusted to the bank by the victims of the Fraudulent Scheme, ie municipalities) became available to the perpetrators, overdrafts were cleared and funds could be transferred out of such accounts Motau found that the contract financing was a prime location of the looting of the funds of VBS. “Astonishingly, the contract finance book, which eventually became the single largest asset of VBS was not recorded in the bank’s operating system, but was simply recorded on an Excel spreadsheet which could be manipulated with ease. “The inescapable inference that must be drawn from this is that it better suited the interest of those who sought to manipulate VBS’ banking systems for their own benefit to keep contract finance off the operating system.” WHOSE MONEY WAS USED? This fraudulent mechanism provided the perpetrators and their associated entities, including Vele, with money which was predominantly made of deposits held by the bank on behalf of members of the public and municipalities. THIS, they used to fund their lifestyles, purchase immovable property, buy high-end motor vehicles and take up shares and interests in other entities. CATEGORIES OF FRAUDULENT TRANSACTIONS PERPETRATED THROUGH SCHEME VELE’S INSURE ACQUISITION: R250 MILLION Vele fraudulently acquired an investment in Insure Group Managers (Pty) Ltd for an amount of R250 million. The acquisition was funded by VBS through the Fraudulent Scheme - in other words, Vele paid nothing for the investment. (add more to this paragraphs 108 - 115) 2. VELE’S PURPORTED SHARE UPTAKES IN VBS (R80 MILLION & R90 MILLION) Vele purported to purchase shares in VBS on two occassions in order to become the majority shareholder: First: Vele fraudulently misrepresented that an actual R80 million deposit made by Insure into VBS for an unrelated purpose, was payment of the purchase price in respect of a share subscription in VBS. Neither Vele, nor Insure on its behalf, paid any money For the shares. Second: Vele purported to subscribe for further shares in VBS, by paying the amount of R90 million with the proceeds for a fictitious deposit of R350 million created through the Fraudulent Scheme. Again, Vele paid nothing for these shares. Motau stated that Vele was an “ostensible” shareholder shareholder in VBS. He found that during 2017 Vele purported to take up a 53% shareholding in VBS. This was purportedly in terms of a rights issue. Vele, which was not an existing shareholder at the time of the rights issue, was therefore not entitled to take up any shares on offer. However, Vele managed to convince the board of directors of VBS to accept an amount of R80 million as an equity investment against the issue of a majority shareholding. In truth, Vele invested absolutely nothing into VBS and it acquired the shares by a blatant fraud. (See further Motau report page 58 & 59) 3. FRAUDULENT OVERDRAFT PAYMENTS: R262 MILLION The Fraudulent Scheme was used to clear - or repay - the outstanding overdraft facilities in respect of Matodzi, other perpetrators and their associated entities in an amount of approximately R262 million. These fraudulent transactions which will also be referenced as the “Eagle Canyon List” (so named after the meeting at Eagle Canyon where Matodzi instructed the clearing of overdrafts). (more in paragraphs 116 - 289) Motau noted (p 57) there are many examples of vehicle finance facilities and mortgage bond facilities granted to associates and parties related to Vele and Matodzi where few, if any, monthly instalments were honoured. There are also very large overdraft facilities where no amounts were ever paid into the accounts and the facility limits simply increased to permit the escalating out flows. 4. Fraudulent deposits: R929 925 280.46 Fraudulently created deposits were made through the Fraudelent Scheme to several of the perpetrators and their associated entities. Vele was the recipient of the bulk of these fraudulent deposits in the amount of R745 million. WHY THE BANK GOT INTO TROUBLE The deficit created by the perpetrators grew larger as the perpetrators were effectively stealing money at a greater rate than was being deposited into VBS. THIS resulted in the severe liquidity crisis in which VBS found itself - which the perpetrators sought to hide in VBS’ 2017 Annual Financial Statements audited by KPMG. The corruption was so deeply entrenched amongst the perpetrators at VBS that they resorted to obtaining deposits into the bank from municipalities by paying officials “commissions” on funds deposited by municipalities into VBS. These bribes were channelled through Robvet (pty) Ltd. -- THE LIMPOPO LINK The provincial government of Limpopo has its own internal investigation into how municipal moneys were siphoned into VBS even though the Municipal Finance Mangement Act forbids municipalities from investing money in a mutual bank. ANC Limpopo Treasurer Danny Msiza and ANC Limpopo Deputy Chairperson Florence Radzilani is implicated in the Motau report. The motau report states that during the investigation, Phopi Londolani Mukhodobwane - VBS General Head of Treasury and Capital Management - testified, that the kingpin in the so-called “commission agent” scheme was Msiza. It is said that Msiza that commission of 2-3% for soliciting municipality agents to deposit money with VBS Bank. Limpopo ANC Spokesperson Ntshaveni Khumbudzo (060-769-0338) said that its internal report would only be complete at the end of November. They say they will act against officials implicated. FURTHER ATTEMPTS TO SAVE THE BANK FROM IMPLODING Further attempts were made to obtain deposits from the PIC and PRASA (R1 billion). The Motau report states: To avoid the bank from imploding after municipalities withdrew deposits, VBS went on an ambitious campaign to attract other large deposits from municipalities and state-owed entities like the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) and shifted towards aggressive, high-risk lending. During the investigation, key witness General Manager of Treasury at VBS, Phopi Mukhodobwane, testified that VBS had attempted to solicit R1-billion from Prasa in late 2017. The report states that Mukhodobwane testified that a “commission” - read “bribe” - of R1,5-million was paid to a group of union officials from Satawu who claimed to be able to facilitate such a large deposit from Prasa. The plan was stymied thanks to an unrelated investigation into Prasa. Mukhodobwane himself stole R30-million from the bank, Motau and Werksmans found.
